UGT1A1 inhibitors, such as atazanavir, reduce the metabolism of irinotecan, leading to increased levels or effects of liposomal irinotecan by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 2. UGT1A1 inhibitors, including atazanavir, decrease the metabolism of ivosidenib, resulting in elevated levels or effects of ivosidenib through hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme interactions. Avoid coadministration or use alternative therapies. If coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the ivosidenib dose to 250 mg daily. Upon discontinuation of the strong inhibitor (after at least 5 half-lives), increase the ivosidenib dose to the recommended 500 mg daily. 3. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of larotrectinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 4. Atazanavir increases lefamulin levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration of lefamulin with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 5. Atazanavir increases lemborexant levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration of lemborexant with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. 6. Atazanavir increases lenacapavir levels or effects through mechanisms involving P-gp, UGT1A1, and strong CYP3A inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 7. Atazanavir increases leniolisib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 8. Atazanavir, levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate, and hormonal contraceptives may interact, causing significant changes in estrogen plasma levels and reducing contraceptive efficacy. Use nonhormonal contraceptives instead. 9. Lopinavir increases atazanavir levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 10. Atazanavir increases lorlatinib levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce lorlatinib dose by 25 mg/day. Upon discontinuation of the strong inhibitor (after 3 plasma half-lives), resume the previous lorlatinib dose. 11. Atazanavir increases levels or effects of lovotibeglogene autotemcel. Discontinue antiretrovirals (ARTs) at least 1 month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Long-acting ARTs may require longer discontinuation periods to avoid interference with manufacturing. 12. Atazanavir increases lurbinectedin levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the lurbinectedin dose by 50%. After discontinuing the strong CYP3A inhibitor for 5 half-lives, resume the previous lurbinectedin dose. 13. Atazanavir increases macitentan levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 14. Magnesium oxide decreases atazanavir levels or effects by increasing gastric pH. Administer atazanavir 2 hours before or 1 hour after magnesium oxide. 15. Atazanavir increases mefloquine levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Mefloquine may enhance QTc prolongation effects of high-risk agents. 16. Atazanavir increases methylergonovine levels by decreasing metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 17. Atazanavir increases midazolam levels by decreasing metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 18. Atazanavir increases intranasal midazolam levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may prolong sedation. 19. Atazanavir increases midostaurin levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, monitor for increased adverse reactions, especially during the first week of treatment. 20. Atazanavir increases modafinil levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 21. Atazanavir increases nefazodone levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 22. Atazanavir increases neratinib levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 23. Atazanavir increases nevirapine levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 24. Atazanavir increases nirogacestat levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 25. Nizatidine decreases atazanavir levels or effects by increasing gastric pH. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Administer atazanavir simultaneously with H2-receptor antagonists (H2RAs) or at least 10 hours afterward in treatment-naïve patients. 26. Atazanavir increases olaparib levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with moderate CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the olaparib dose to 200 mg (capsule) or 150 mg (tablet) twice daily. Do not substitute tablets with capsules. 27. Atazanavir increases omaveloxolone levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 50 mg/day. Monitor closely and discontinue if adverse effects emerge. 28. Omeprazole decreases atazanavir levels or effects by increasing gastric pH. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Administer omeprazole 12 hours before atazanavir/ritonavir in treatment-naïve patients. PPIs are not recommended in treatment-experienced patients taking atazanavir. 29. Atazanavir increases osimertinib levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If no alternatives exist, monitor closely for adverse effects. 30. Atazanavir increases oxycodone levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction may be warranted when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 31. Atazanavir increases palbociclib levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day. 32. Atazanavir increases palovarotene levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 33. Pantoprazole decreases atazanavir levels or effects by increasing gastric pH. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Administer pantoprazole 12 hours before atazanavir/ritonavir in treatment-naïve patients. PPIs are not recommended in treatment-experienced patients taking atazanavir. 34. Atazanavir increases pazopanib levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the pazopanib dose to 400 mg/day. 35. Atazanavir increases pemigatinib levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pemigatinib dose as per drug monograph recommendations. 36. Atazanavir increases pexidartinib levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per drug monograph recommendations. 37. Atazanavir increases pimavanserin levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the pimavanserin dose to 17 mg/day if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 38. Atazanavir increases pirtobrutinib levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the pirtobrutinib dose by 50 mg. If the current dose is 50 mg daily, discontinue pirtobrutinib during strong CYP3A inhibitor use. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 5 half-lives. 39. Atazanavir increases pomalidomide levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 40. Atazanavir increases ponatinib levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the ponatinib starting dose to 30 mg daily if coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided. 41. Atazanavir increases pralsetinib levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 42. Atazanavir increases quetiapine levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider alternative anti-HCV therapy to avoid increased quetiapine exposure. If coadministration is necessary, reduce the quetiapine dose to one-sixth of the current dose and monitor for adverse reactions. 43. Rabeprazole decreases atazanavir levels or effects by increasing gastric pH. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Administer rabeprazole 12 hours before atazanavir/ritonavir in treatment-naïve patients. PPIs are not recommended in treatment-experienced patients taking atazanavir. 44. Atazanavir increases ranolazine levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 45. Atazanavir increases red yeast rice levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Red yeast rice contains monacolin K, which may increase the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis. 46. Atazanavir increases repotrectinib levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Discontinue strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors and wait 3-5 elimination half-lives before initiating repotrectinib. 47. Atazanavir increases resmetirom levels or effects. Avoid coadministration of resmetirom (an OATP1B1/3 substrate) with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors. 48. Atazanavir increases ribociclib levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with a strong CYP3A inhibitor is necessary, reduce the ribociclib starting dose to 400 mg/day. 49. Rifampin decreases atazanavir levels or effects by altering hepatic metabolism. Avoid coadministration.
